description: Circuitscape is open-source software that models landscape connectivity with electronic circuit theory: it treats a landscape as a resistance surface and computes current flow between habitat patches over all possible pathways at once. Companion tools are Omniscape for omnidirectional connectivity in a moving window, Linkage Mapper for least-cost corridors, pinch points and barriers, and Gnarly Landscape Utilities for resistance layers. It was created by Brad McRae, Viral Shah, Tanmay Mohapatra and Ranjan Anantharaman, and version 5 was rewritten in Julia with NASA and The Nature Conservancy support. Coverage is any landscape the user supplies as rasters, at their resolution. Format and access: downloads and documentation on the website. Licence: stated as free and open source, without the licence named on the home page; free. Caveats: results depend strongly on resistance values chosen by the user, and it models movement of organisms or flows, not engineered hydraulics. For green and blue infrastructure it is used to design ecological corridors and green networks and to test how development fragments them, a network flow analysis. A related catalogue record is the Natural England Green Infrastructure Mapping Database, whose layers can form the resistance surface.
